conclusions: Manual monitoring creates detection lag and silent policy drift.
A reliable control needs normalized agency identity, observed-at timestamps, automated diffs, and accountable exceptions.
counterarguments: An improved manual review cadence could reduce lag without vendor integration.
findings: Flock told The Dispatch it does not maintain the 287(g) classification.
More than 400 agencies reportedly retained access after national sharing was disabled.
One pre-existing agreement was missed and three newly ineligible partners remained until press inquiry.
limitations: No evidence was found that ICE publishes a stable change feed suitable for direct automation.
data.question: Can CPD reliably maintain the exclusion using periodic manual review across hundreds of partner agencies?
recommendations: Build and test a reconciliation actor.
Publish signed edge snapshots and revocation reasons.
Alert on every status or sharing-edge change.
